descVi: Thi đấu, tinh thần đồng đội, kỷ luật và rèn luyện thể lực.

words.definitionEn: to hit someone or something with a closed hand
words.exampleDailyEn: She punched the training bag, then caught her breath.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Boxers learn to deliver a controlled punch while maintaining balance and protecting themselves from injury.

words.definitionEn: Someone who watches an event, especially a sporting event.
words.exampleDailyEn: A spectator caught the ball near the fence.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Major sporting events attract thousands of spectators and can generate substantial income for local businesses.

words.definitionEn: An important victory or impressive achievement.
words.exampleDailyEn: Winning the local chess tournament was a triumph for Amir.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The successful restoration of the wetland represents a triumph for conservation groups and local residents.

words.definitionEn: Someone who pursues an activity for pleasure rather than pay.
words.exampleDailyEn: Although an amateur, she takes beautiful photographs of birds.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Amateur sports clubs provide affordable opportunities for physical activity and help strengthen relationships within local communities.

words.definitionEn: the sport or skill of shooting arrows with a bow
words.exampleDailyEn: We tried archery at a supervised outdoor activity centre.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Offering archery in schools could introduce students to a sport that develops concentration and physical coordination.

words.meaningVi: Một sợi dây co giãn chắc chắn dùng để cố định đồ vật hoặc nhảy bungee
words.definitionEn: A strong stretchy cord used for securing objects or bungee jumping.
words.exampleDailyEn: We secured the sleeping bags with a strong bungee.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Adventure tourism operators must inspect every bungee cord regularly to ensure that essential safety standards are maintained.

words.definitionEn: a building where club members meet and use shared facilities
words.exampleDailyEn: We left our tennis bags outside the clubhouse.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A shared clubhouse can strengthen community ties by giving local sports teams a place to meet regularly.

words.definitionEn: a person who fights in battle or combat sports
words.exampleDailyEn: The young fighter practises footwork with her coach every morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A successful fighter needs disciplined training, adequate recovery, and access to professional medical support.

words.definitionEn: Riding a board across water while pulled by a kite.
words.exampleDailyEn: My cousin tried kitesurfing at the beach yesterday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Coastal resorts offering kitesurfing should separate training areas from swimming zones to reduce accidents.

words.definitionEn: A long pole with a flat blade for rowing boats
words.exampleDailyEn: He lifted one oar and gently pushed the boat away.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Visitors can explore the lake in traditional boats, using oars rather than engines to minimise disturbance to wildlife.

words.definitionEn: An area of ground used for outdoor team sports.
words.exampleDailyEn: The players ran onto the pitch despite the rain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Young entrepreneurs often pitch their business ideas to investors who can provide funding and practical guidance.

words.definitionEn: Done for enjoyment and relaxation rather than work.
words.exampleDailyEn: The lake is a popular spot for recreational fishing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Providing affordable recreational facilities can improve public health and strengthen social connections within urban communities.

words.definitionEn: a race in which teammates take turns completing sections
words.exampleDailyEn: Our team dropped the baton during the school relay.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Emergency services relay weather warnings to remote communities through local radio stations and mobile networks.

words.definitionEn: a seat on a horse or bicycle
words.exampleDailyEn: I lowered the saddle before riding my new bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Excessive university fees can saddle graduates with debts that limit their career choices for many years.

words.definitionEn: Someone sent to gather information or discover talented people.
words.exampleDailyEn: A scout watched our team practise after school.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Sports clubs often scout for talented young players in communities that lack access to professional training facilities.

words.definitionEn: protecting yourself from attack or physical harm
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister attends a self-defence class every Saturday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Self-defence courses can build confidence, although avoiding dangerous situations should remain the primary focus of personal safety.

words.definitionEn: against an opponent, or compared with another option
words.exampleDailyEn: Tonight's match is our school versus the local college.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The debate over public versus private transport often centres on cost, convenience, and environmental impact.
collocations: the case of A versus B

words.definitionEn: An achievement requiring great skill, strength, or courage.
words.exampleDailyEn: Carrying that huge sofa upstairs was quite a feat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Building a railway across mountainous terrain remains an impressive feat of engineering, even with modern technology.

words.definitionEn: The ability to continue despite tiredness, pain, or difficulty.
words.exampleDailyEn: Swimming every morning has really improved my endurance.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity builds endurance and helps people manage the demands of an increasingly sedentary lifestyle.

words.definitionEn: A strap used by a rider to guide a horse.
words.exampleDailyEn: The rider gently pulled the reins to stop the horse.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may need to rein in excessive spending while protecting essential services such as education and healthcare.

words.definitionEn: Fair and respectful behaviour towards opponents in sport
words.exampleDailyEn: Helping her opponent up showed real sportsmanship.
words.exampleIeltsEn: School competitions should reward sportsmanship as well as achievement to encourage respect and cooperation among students.

words.definitionEn: Having won a competition, battle, or struggle.
words.exampleDailyEn: The victorious team lifted the trophy above their heads.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Athletes who emerge victorious in international competitions often inspire younger generations to participate in sport.

words.definitionEn: a hit or kick before the ball touches the ground
words.exampleDailyEn: She won the tennis match with a sharp volley.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Learning to volley effectively helps young tennis players develop coordination and respond quickly under pressure.

words.definitionEn: to defeat an opponent completely
words.exampleDailyEn: Our chess club finally vanquished its strongest rival yesterday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health campaigns cannot vanquish widespread misinformation without sustained cooperation between educators, researchers, and local communities.

words.definitionEn: Straps fitted around a horse's head to control it.
words.exampleDailyEn: She checked the horse's bridle before climbing into the saddle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some employees bridle at strict monitoring policies because they feel their professional judgement is being questioned.
